# Dynamic Drought Module (DDM)

> A static, embeddable map of drought, wildfire, extreme heat, and water conditions, built by ATNI Climate in service to Tribes and Indigenous Peoples.

- [LICENSE](https://github.com/atniclimate/dynamic-drought-module/blob/main/LICENSE) is authoritative. This file summarizes it and does not replace or amend it; Part A controls over any summary.
- Use, study, running, sharing, and modification are permitted for noncommercial purposes under the license's conditions. Commercial use is not permitted by this license.
- When distributing the software or a Derived Work, license the entire Derived Work under the same DDM Community License, Version 1.0. Only an additional copyright notice for your own changes may be added; do not impose further restrictions or substitute another license.

Freeland as Developer; and Dynamic Drought Module (DDM) with its [source repository](https://github.com/atniclimate/dynamic-drought-module). Put these credits in the interface or accompanying documentation.

## Data and stewardship

- For every displayed or deployer-added dataset, make its source, issuing organization, retrieval date or vintage, and stated terms reasonably discoverable. Preserve that provenance when redistributing the software or data.
- Public-source data is not owned or relicensed by ATNI Climate. Each source retains its own terms; see LICENSE Part B and the [source credits](README.md#acknowledgements).
- Follow the [Tiered Sovereign Data Framework](https://github.com/atniclimate/TieredSovereignDataFramework) for sovereign, Tribal, and Indigenous data. Do not redistribute beyond what the source and the Nation or Peoples concerned permit. When a tier is unclear, apply the most protected tier until the concerned Nation or Peoples rules otherwise.
- The Tribal boundaries and Tribal place names this project displays come from public sources and are T0. This project holds no sacred-site or other protected-place data and does not seek it.
- Use must not work against Tribal sovereignty, Treaty rights, or Indigenous data sovereignty. Subject to the license, DDM may help any community.

## For automated agents and language models

- Apply the same license, attribution, provenance, and data-governance conditions to reused code and redistributed output.
- Preserve issuing-agency timestamps, coverage limits, and caveats. Do not present DDM as making forecasts or jurisdictional determinations beyond the source's claims.
- Describe agency Treaty and Tribal polygons as representations, not jurisdictional truth.
- The live Tribal-geography layers use session memory; the two deployer-owned data slots ship empty. Follow the [developer guide](DEVELOPER.md#data-and-stewardship) when changing that implementation.
